newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - German shares hit new record, franc falters.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - German shares hit new record, franc falters.

text.p: German shares stormed to a new record close on Thursday and French stocks also surged after comments by a Bank of France policymaker pushed the dollar higher against the franc and the mark.
Bank of France monetary policy council member Jean-Pierre Gerard said in an interview with Le Monde he wanted a stronger dollar against the mark, implying a desire for a weaker franc.
One way to get the dollar higher would be to cut short-term rates in France and Germany, making equities more attractive.

"Unfortunately we have little influence on German monetary policy," he was quoted as saying. "A second possibility, given that we cannot get a concerted reduction in rates, would be to modify the franc-mark parity."

Analysts said the French government needs a higher dollar/mark rate to resolve economic problems highlighted in the domestic debate about foreign exchange policy but it also needs the collusion of the Bundesbank to achieve it.
Critics of French exchange rate policy believe the dollar is undervalued against the German mark and the franc, slowing French growth and employment by giving U.S. exports an edge.
Around 1630 gmt, the franc stood at 3.3927 per mark having been as low as 3.3972 earlier and compared with 3.3860 late on Wednesday, and at 5.2006 against the dollar after 5.1725.

French shares ended almost 0.9 percent higher, slightly off their day's best and just shy of key resistance around 2,300. Prices shot up during the morning as the franc fell versus the dollar boosting the outlook for exporters.
Germany's DAX index of 30 top shares ended bourse trade at a record closing high, after the dollar raced to its highest level for a month against the mark.
The DAX index closed at 2,817.49 points, up 0.73 percent, or 20.46 points, just below its all-time intraday record high of 2,819.95 points reached on Tuesday.
The dollar penetrated the 1.53 mark level, after Gerard's comments, particularly benefiting Germany's export-oriented chemicals and auto sectors.
But dealers said volumes were somewhat dampened due to the Thanksgiving holiday in the United States.
In after hours trading the DAX Ibis index was up more that 1.28 percent, or 35.82 points, at 2,829.68 points.
Shares in Europe's biggest carmaker Volkswagen AG continued to be at the centre of attention and recovered two percent, closing bourse dealings up 11.70 marks at 613 marks.

In London, shares ended a sliver higher after weakness in drug stocks kept the FTSE-100 index in the minus column for most of the day. Strength on continental bourses and strong gilts gave the market some impetus on what was a quiet day with Wall Street's absence for the Thanksgiving Day holiday.
Traders said the market was likely to be marooned near its current levels with Wall Street unlikely to see much action in tomorrow's shortened post-holiday session.
The dollar held onto most of its early gains against the yen on the back of the Bank of Japan's uninspiring quarterly Tankan report of business confidence on Wednesday.

In metals, Copper prices rose above $2,300 a tonne, the highest since the Sumitomo Corp scandal erupted in June, as critically low inventory levels forced buyers to scramble for metal, traders and analysts said, though it later fell back.
During the morning gold was fixed at $372.20, its lowest fix in over 2-1/2 years, as soaring stock markets and the stronger dollar pulled cash out of bullion. Prices rallied later however.
Oil prices fell a touch on news that Iraqi crude oil would start flowing through the trans-Turkey pipeline by December 15.

International benchmark Brent Blend crude from the North Sea fell 15 cents after the news to $22.60 a barrel, down 12 cents on the day. Earlier it rose to $22.89 after OPEC ministers in Vienna agreed to freeze production to the end of June 1997.
CURRENCIES AT 1645 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 113.62 yen and 1.5320 marks against 113.33 yen and 1.5275 marks in late Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 1.0 point at 4,050.2.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 19.54 at 2,290.31.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 20.46 at 2817.49.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold ended around $372.65 up from the morning's fix of $372.20, the lowest fix since April 25, 1994, and against $373.75 late on Wednesday.
